newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-STRICKEN FRENCH SOLO YACHTSMAN RESCUED.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-STRICKEN FRENCH SOLO YACHTSMAN RESCUED.

text.p: French solo yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued on Friday in the Southern Ocean by a fellow competitor in the round-the-world Vendee Globe race, an Australian rescue official said.
Dinelli abandoned his sinking yacht Algimouss some 1,200 nautical miles southwest of Western Australia after a search aircraft dropped him a life raft on Thursday.
Briton Pete Goss was re-routed to rescue Dinelli, 28, and picked him up in his yacht Aqua Quorum on Friday morning, said the Australian Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre.
"The search aircraft relocated the life raft this morning and the yachtsman had been picked up by Aqua Quorum," the official told Reuters.
"He is okay, but suffering from hypothermia," he said.
Goss plans to take Dinelli to the Australian southern island state of Tasmania, said the rescue official.
"This would allow him to continue in the race. If he was to go to Perth in Western Australia it would be a big detour."
An Australian airforce official said the Orion search aircraft was circling the Aqua Quorum to ensure all was well with both yachtsmen.

Dinelli, who was out of radio contact, set off distress signals early on Thursday morning as his 18.3 metre (60 foot) yacht met heavy seas and winds in the roaring 40s which blow from South Africa to Australia.

He abandoned his half-submerged yacht, which was being battered by winds of up to 40 knots and heavy seas, after an Australian airforce plane dropped him a life raft containing food and communication equipment. Weather conditions in the area improved overnight.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier, who was competing in the same race.

She was eventually winched from her dismasted yacht in an operation criticised by the Australian media because Australian taxpayers and not race organisers had to foot the rescue bill, estimated at up to A$1 million ($790,000).
